## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode #14557 research-worktree-session-binding-strategy - HIGH PRIORITY (agent-manager + config)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14557 "fix(agent-manager): survive inaccessible historical project paths" merged 2026-09-25 fixed project-scoped provider/config caching (previously, cached providers and config payloads were not keyed to the directory they were loaded for, so switching to a new project whose bootstrap failed could silently reuse the previous project's config and providers; fix keys the cached state to the directory, so retryInitialization means "bootstrapped for this project" rather than "bootstrapped for any project"; also guards SessionTranscript scope resolution against retained inaccessible sandbox paths - filesystem.resolve throws EACCES/EPERM for such paths, which previously could die when attaching a past chat; unresolvable paths now treated as out of scope, matching session family resolution). This is agent-manager config isolation (per-project provider/config caching prevents silent cross-project reuse).

- **Why**: Alexi has agent-manager worktree support (src/core/agent-manager/, src/tool/tools/agent-manager.ts, agent-manager.json state) but may lack per-project config/provider caching — switching worktrees could silently reuse the wrong project's SAP AI Core credentials, routing config, or model catalog (src/config/alexi.ts loads config from cwd, but cached provider state in src/providers/index.ts is global). Kilocode's fix prevents config leakage by keying the cache to the resolved project path, and retries config/provider initialization when Agent Manager activates a project (so a healthy project recovers without restart when initial bootstrap failed). Implementation path: audit agent-manager project switching (src/core/agent-manager/, find where config/providers are initialized per worktree), check if cached provider state (src/providers/index.ts, getProviderForModel) is keyed to project path or global, add project-scoped provider/config cache (key by resolved cwd), retry provider init on worktree activation (when initial bootstrap failed), guard against inaccessible historical paths in session scope resolution (src/core/sessionManager.ts or src/core/sessionContext.ts, catch EACCES/EPERM from filesystem.resolve), write tests (config cache isolated per project, worktree switch does not leak previous config, inaccessible path treated as out of scope).

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14557 (Kilocode project-scoped config caching, merged 2026-09-25), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/agent-manager/ (Alexi agent-manager), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/index.ts (Alexi provider dispatch, audit for global vs project-scoped cache), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/config/alexi.ts (Alexi config loading)

- **Category**: agent-manager + config (per-project provider/config caching, session scope guard)

- **Size**: MEDIUM (~6-10h). Audit agent-manager project switching (src/core/agent-manager/, find where providers/config initialized per worktree), audit provider cache scope (src/providers/index.ts, check if getProviderForModel caches per project or globally), add project-scoped cache (key provider/config cache by resolved cwd, clear on project switch), add retry-on-activation (when Agent Manager activates a worktree, retry provider/config init if bootstrap previously failed), guard session scope resolution (src/core/sessionManager.ts or sessionContext.ts, catch EACCES/EPERM from filesystem.resolve, treat as out of scope), write tests (worktree switch isolates config, failed bootstrap recovers on activation, inaccessible path handled).

#### 2. Kilocode #13808 Close Task/Close All Tasks commands - MEDIUM PRIORITY (tui + cli)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #13808 "feat(vscode): add Close Task and Close All Tasks commands" merged 2026-09-25 added bulk task close commands (Close Task closes focused task tab, Close All Tasks closes every visible task tab and returns to empty start state; both work in sidebar, editor tabs, and Agent Manager; bulk close stops sessions in single abort batch and leaves terminals/reviews/worktrees untouched; commands route to the Kilo surface the user last worked in; sessions leave Agent Manager state before processes are stopped so concurrent state push cannot restore tabs just closed; Agent Manager gained per-project suppression of closed Local sessions; bulk close loops the tab bar's own close handler so suppression/draft cleanup/focus restore stay in one place). This is multi-session lifecycle management (bulk close with proper cleanup, per-project closed-session suppression).

- **Why**: Alexi CLI has multi-session capability (src/core/sessionManager.ts, src/cli/tui/), but no bulk-close UX — users must exit sessions one by one (Ctrl+C, then resume another), and no explicit "close all active sessions" command exists. Kilocode's Close All Tasks pattern (bulk abort batch, per-project suppression, single cleanup handler) informs future multi-session management: if Alexi gains a session-switcher UI or concurrent session view (like agent-manager's worktree grid), the bulk-close lifecycle (stop sessions in batch, suppress closed sessions per project, leave worktrees/terminals intact) becomes relevant. LOW IMMEDIATE PRIORITY (Alexi TUI is single-session-at-a-time today, no tab grid), but MEDIUM for future multi-session UX. Document pattern for future reference.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13808 (Kilocode bulk task close, merged 2026-09-25), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/sessionManager.ts (Alexi session manager), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/tui/ (Alexi TUI)

- **Category**: tui + cli (multi-session lifecycle, bulk close pattern)

- **Size**: MEDIUM (~4-6h when needed). Today Alexi TUI is single-session (one chat at a time, no tab grid), so no immediate implementation. Document the pattern (bulk abort batch, per-project closed-session suppression, single cleanup handler) for when Alexi gains concurrent session view or agent-manager-style worktree grid. If implementing: add bulk-close command (src/cli/commands/, stop sessions in single abort batch), add per-project closed-session suppression (track closed session IDs per project root, suppress in session list), leave worktrees/terminals untouched (only stop session processes), write tests (bulk close stops all sessions, suppression prevents restore, terminals/worktrees intact).

#### 3. Kilocode #14502 session cleanup sub-agent retention - MEDIUM PRIORITY (core + retention)

- **What**: Kilocode commit "fix(cli): keep sub-agents of a chat in use during session cleanup" (2026-09-25) fixed session cleanup logic to retain sub-agents of active parent sessions (previously, cleanup sweep could delete sub-agents while their parent chat was still in use; fix keeps the entire session family — parent + descendants — when parent is active). This is retention policy (session cleanup respects session family hierarchy, does not orphan active parents by deleting their sub-agents).

- **Why**: Alexi has retention scheduler (src/core/retentionScheduler.ts, configured via retention policy in config) and session hierarchy (parent-child sessions via task tool, tracked in session metadata). Kilocode's fix highlights a gap: does Alexi's cleanup sweep retain sub-agents of active parent sessions, or only the parent itself? If the retention policy only checks the parent's lastAccessedAt, sub-agents spawned by the parent (e.g. task tool background agents) could be deleted while the parent is still running, breaking the parent's ability to read task results. Implementation path: audit retention sweep (src/core/retentionScheduler.ts, check if it walks session families or only filters by lastAccessedAt), add session family retention (when a parent is retained, retain all descendants recursively), write tests (active parent's sub-agents are retained, inactive family deleted together).

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/commits (Kilocode commit "fix(cli): keep sub-agents of a chat in use during session cleanup", 2026-09-25), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/retentionScheduler.ts (Alexi retention scheduler), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/sessionManager.ts (Alexi session hierarchy tracking)

- **Category**: core + retention (session cleanup, family hierarchy)

- **Size**: SMALL (~2-4h). Audit retention sweep (src/core/retentionScheduler.ts, check if retention policy walks session families or only filters by lastAccessedAt), add family retention logic (when a parent session is retained by policy, recursively retain all descendants tracked in session metadata), write tests (active parent's sub-agents retained, inactive family deleted together, orphaned sub-agents cleaned up).

#### 4. Kilocode #13523 TUI offline watchdog - MEDIUM PRIORITY (tui + core)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #13523 "fix(cli): surface network disconnects in the TUI instead of hanging silently" merged 2026-09-25 added TUI offline watchdog (session already paused/resumed on network drop, but TUI never rendered offline status and mid-request disconnect could blackhole connection with infinite spinner; fix renders offline status in prompt's inline error line "<message> [waiting for network]" and adds per-attempt watchdog: after 10s of stream silence, probe connectivity and fail attempt with disconnect error so it lands in existing offline flow; passing probe or in-flight tool call resets clock so slow providers and long-running tools never tripped; local/private endpoints probed directly via TCP connect, remote providers use public-host probe; probe lookup bounded and expansion of env vars in probe URL handled; late probe rejections and deadline timer cleanup hardened). This is TUI reliability (network disconnect surfacing, stream-silence watchdog prevents infinite hang).

- **Why**: Alexi has TUI (src/cli/tui/), streamWatchdog (src/core/streamWatchdog.ts), and network manager (src/core/network.ts) but may lack the stream-silence probe pattern — a mid-request disconnect or a stalled provider (no chunks, no error) may hang the TUI with infinite spinner instead of surfacing "[waiting for network]" inline error. Kilocode's watchdog: 10s stream silence → probe connectivity → fail attempt if unreachable, reset clock if probe passes or tool executing. Alexi's streamWatchdog exists but audit: does it probe connectivity on silence, or only detect already-known offline state? Implementation path: audit streamWatchdog (src/core/streamWatchdog.ts, check if it probes connectivity after stream silence or only reacts to NetworkManager offline events), add stream-silence watchdog (10s no-chunk timer, probe connectivity on timeout, fail attempt with disconnect error if unreachable, reset timer on chunk or tool-call-start), add local endpoint TCP probe (resolve provider baseURL, if localhost/LAN/bare hostname probe via TCP connect, else use public-host probe), integrate with TUI (src/cli/tui/, render "[waiting for network]" inline error when attempt fails with disconnect), write tests (stream silence → probe → disconnect error, passing probe resets timer, tool execution holds timer, local endpoint probed directly).

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13523 (Kilocode TUI offline watchdog, merged 2026-09-25), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/streamWatchdog.ts (Alexi stream watchdog, audit), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/network.ts (Alexi network manager), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/tui/ (Alexi TUI rendering)

- **Category**: tui + core (stream watchdog, network disconnect surfacing)

- **Size**: MEDIUM (~6-8h). Audit streamWatchdog (src/core/streamWatchdog.ts, check if it probes on stream silence or only reacts to offline events), add stream-silence probe (10s no-chunk timer, on timeout probe connectivity - local endpoints via TCP, remote via public hosts, fail attempt with disconnect error if unreachable, reset on chunk/tool-call-start), integrate into TUI (src/cli/tui/, render "[waiting for network]" in prompt inline error when disconnect detected), add provider endpoint resolution (resolve provider baseURL from model, expand env vars, detect local vs remote), write tests (stream silence triggers probe, disconnect surfaces error, passing probe keeps attempt alive, tool execution holds timer).
